STEP 1 - Scene: A single whole apple (red-yellow, likely a gala or similar variety) resting on a white square-ish dinner plate, photographed from directly above. There is a small smear of residue (possibly juice or sauce) near the top of the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-rimmed white dish about 26 cm across its widest diagonal-free span. Taking the straight-edge width of about 26 cm as the diameter-equivalent, area ≈ 3.14 × (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm². The apple is roughly 7.5 cm in diameter by visual scale against the plate.

STEP 3 - Items: One whole apple. Small residue smear (negligible, under 1 g).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's top-down projected area is about π × (3.75)^2 ≈ 44 cm², roughly 8% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: An apple is roughly spherical, so volume ≈ (4/3)π(3.75)^3 ≈ 220 ml. Since it is a whole fruit rather than cut pieces, its real volume is close to this envelope, so I use about 220 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A whole apple's density is close to 1.0 g/ml, not the cut-fruit bulk density, so ≈ 200 g. Typical medium apples weigh 150–200 g; this one looks mid-sized, so I estimate about 170 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Raw apple ≈ 52 kcal/100 g. 170 g × 0.52 ≈ 88 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple at ~170 g and ~90 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The residue is negligible. The plate is mostly empty, consistent with a single fruit.
